findings.description: The `if (amounts[i] > 0)` skip guard at :134 filters on the PRE-deposit snapshot credit, but the revert it is documented (section (D), :39-47) to prevent lives on the POST-deposit quantity. StableStaker.depositFor:641-642 computes `credited = _routeDeposit(token, received)` — which for a wired strategy is `strategy.deposit(...)`, free to floor a dust amount to 0 share-units — and then `require(credited > 0, "StableStaker: nothing credited")`. A user with amounts[i] == 1 wei therefore passes the migrator's guard and reverts the ENTIRE batch inside the destination staker. The guard only covers the case where the OLD staker's floor division produced 0; it does not cover the NEW staker's strategy-side floor. Section (D) explicitly rejects off-chain pre-filtering as 'a landmine', so the documented mitigation is the only one, and it is one-sided.
findings.confidenceNote: High confidence that the guard is on the wrong quantity (mechanical, both sides read). Reachability of credited==0 depends on the destination pool's strategy: trivially reachable for an ERC4626/Tokemak-backed strategy at dust amounts, unreachable when yieldStrategy[token]==0 (idle hold returns `amount` unchanged, StableStaker.sol:769-771).
findings.exploitable: NOT defused. onlyOwner does not help — the owner cannot see credited without simulating, and the whole point of (D) is that batches are built blind from getStakersRange. Impact is DoS/operational, not theft: the batch reverts atomically, no value moves. Owner can work around only by the off-chain pre-filter (D) rejects.

findings.description: CrossVersionMigrator takes physical custody of principal (StableStaker.batchMigrate:521 does `IERC20(token).safeTransfer(msg.sender, total)`) and exposes NO rescue/sweep function. Its own sibling InPlaceMigrator — same repo, same author, same custody model — DOES ship a floor-fenced `rescueERC20` (InPlaceMigrator.sol:338, fenced by `totalParked`), and the contract docs there call that fence load-bearing (section (G)). The retired StableStakerMigrator had no rescue either, so the header's 'strict functional superset' claim (:16) is technically true but carries the omission forward. Two concrete stranding paths: (a) any direct/accidental ERC20 transfer to the migrator is permanently locked; (b) the golden-rule interface (section (A)) lets ANY future staker version implement batchMigrate — if such a version returns an `amounts` array LONGER than `users`, the :122-124 sum includes credits the :133-138 loop never deposits, leaving both a residual `forceApprove` allowance and an unrecoverable token balance.
findings.confidenceNote: Path (a) is certain but low-value. Path (b) is contingent on a future staker version; against StableStaker V2 today `amounts = new uint256[](users.length)` (:511) makes lengths always equal, and a SHORTER array panics out-of-bounds (safe atomic revert). Filed as medium because the contract's stated design goal (:21-25) is explicitly to survive 'an arbitrary number of future staker redesigns' — the no-rescue gap is what makes that forward-compat promise unsafe.
findings.exploitable: Not exploitable by a third party. It is a value-recovery gap, not an attack. onlyOwner/immutable do not mitigate it — they are the reason nothing can be recovered.

findings.description: `initiateMigration` (:107-109) is an unvalidated one-way door. It forwards straight into StableStaker.initiateMigration:433, which irreversibly (a) realizes the entire strategy position, (b) revokes the strategy allowance and sets `yieldStrategy[token] = 0`, (c) freezes emissions, and (d) sets `poolState = Migrating`. The only way back to Active is `finalizeAndReset` (:602), which requires the pool be FULLY drained. Nothing in the migrator — or in step 1 of the flow — checks ANY of the destination preconditions that section (C) (:33-37) declares mandatory: that newStaker has the token registered, that newStaker's `migrator` is set to this contract, that newStaker has phUSD minter rights, or even that `oldStaker != newStaker`. Every one of those is discovered only at the FIRST `migrate` call, i.e. after the old pool is already frozen and de-strategied. Concretely for the aliasing case (constructor :89-96 checks both targets non-zero but NOT `_oldStaker != _newStaker`): a same-address deploy lets `initiateMigration` succeed and then makes EVERY non-empty `migrate` batch revert unconditionally, because depositFor:634 requires `poolState == Active` while the pool is now Migrating. Result: yield stopped, strategy unwired, migration impossible, and the entire user base must be told to self-exit via the permissionless `userMigrate` (:564) at the snapshot haircut and re-stake by hand.
findings.confidenceNote: Mechanically certain: all four preconditions are unchecked and initiateMigration is verified irreversible-without-full-drain. The aliasing sub-case is a strict proof that the failure mode is reachable, not a hypothetical.
findings.exploitable: Not attacker-exploitable — onlyOwner throughout, and the immutable targets genuinely close the compromised-key retarget vector section (B) describes. This is a Law-3 FOOTGUN, not a malicious-owner vector: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that a wiring mistake on the DESTINATION is only detected after the SOURCE has been irreversibly frozen. In scope per CLAUDE.md Law 3 (non-obvious consequence, unknowingly disrupts the whole user base). No funds are stolen; `userMigrate` remains a genuine escape hatch, which is what holds this below High.

manualReview.description: The migrator hands `amounts[i]` to depositFor, but the destination books `credited = _routeDeposit(...)` (StableStaker.sol:641) — i.e. whatever the NEW strategy returns, which for an AMM/ERC4626-backed strategy is amount-minus-execution-skew. Users can therefore be haircut a SECOND time on the destination side, on top of the `min(R,P)/P` snapshot haircut section (E) (:49-57) discloses. Section (E) says 'This contract redeposits exactly what it received and no more' — true of the transfer, silent about the credit. No minCredited / slippage parameter exists on migrate().
manualReview.reasonForManualReview: Almost certainly the same root cause already carried in the ledger as 3d61c9552f (medium, acknowledged, requested-vs-received) / b5218ab2 (medium, submitted, sequential-batch AMM haircut) / 970d7307 (medium, fixed, InPlaceMigrator re-injection underpay). Whether CrossVersionMigrator warrants its own entry or reconciles into 3d61c9552f is a dedup/sanitizer call, not a pattern-tier call. Flagging rather than dropping (Law 1).
manualReview.exploitable: Not attacker-driven; value-leak-through-execution. Impact bounded by destination strategy choice.

manualReview.description: `forceApprove(newStaker, total)` then per-user `depositFor(..., amounts[i])` assumes the migrator holds exactly `total` after batchMigrate's single `safeTransfer`. For a fee-on-transfer token the migrator receives total-minus-fee, and the final depositFor's transferFrom fails on insufficient balance, bricking cross-version migration for that token entirely.
manualReview.reasonForManualReview: C4 treats generic fee-on-transfer as OOS unless such tokens are explicitly in scope; stable-staker is a stablecoin staker with no FoT tokens declared in scope. Recorded, not filed.
manualReview.exploitable: Defused in practice by token selection, not by code.

defusedMatches.verdict: DEFUSED + skipped per note. `forceApprove` (SafeERC20) is used, which zeroes before setting, so the USDT-style non-zero-to-non-zero revert and the classic race are both handled. No HM twist found.

DEFUSED. Approval-vs-spend is EXACT: `total` at :122-124 sums the same `amounts` array the :133-138 loop spends, zero entries contribute 0 to both, and StableStaker._pullToken:750-755 does `safeTransferFrom(from, this, amount)` so each call consumes exactly amounts[i] of allowance. Sum in == sum out => residual allowance is 0. A revert anywhere in the loop unwinds the approve atomically. Contrast InPlaceMigrator's dangling `forceApprove(staker, balanceOf)` (ledger f84992e9) — that defect does NOT exist here.

DEFUSED — all three probe cases handled correctly. (1) EOA / no code: staticcall returns ok=TRUE with empty returndata (the classic trap); `data.length < 32` catches it and returns 1. (2) Self-destructed contract: identical to the EOA case, returns 1. (3) Contract that reverts for an unrelated reason: ok=false, returns 1. Short returndata (<32 bytes) is caught by the same length check, so abi.decode can never revert on truncation. Oversized returndata decodes fine for a single static uint256. Residual: a hostile target returning megabytes of returndata imposes memory-expansion gas cost — unreachable, since both probe targets are `immutable` and owner-chosen at construction.

DEFUSED. Section (F) (:59-62) is accurate: no control flow branches on versionOf; it only decorates the MigratedAcrossVersions event. A lying STAKER_VERSION corrupts the on-chain audit record only, and the targets are immutable and owner-chosen, so there is no adversary in position to lie. Correctly weighed as advisory.

DEFUSED. _exitPosition returns 0 immediately when `info.amount == 0` and zeroes `info.amount` on the first pass, so a repeated address in the same or a later batch yields amounts[i] == 0, contributes 0 to `total`, and is skipped by the :134 guard. No double-credit, no double-mint of pending phUSD (which is also computed from the now-zeroed amount).

DEFUSED. initiateMigration freezes (R, P) once and _updatePool no-ops while Migrating, so `credit = (amt * min(R,P)) / P` is identical regardless of batch order, batch size, or whether the user exits via batchMigrate or userMigrate. This is the design property the whole terminal-migration model rests on and it holds.

DEFUSED. Multiplication precedes division (so not DIVISION-PRECISION either), and the floor rounds AGAINST the user / toward the protocol, which is the safe direction. The resulting dust is the acknowledged L-01/ss12l1 item that section (D) documents.

DEFUSED. depositFor follows the correct MasterChef order: _updatePool -> _settle(existing position) -> mutate amount/totalStaked -> recompute rewardDebt from the NEW amount. No accrual is stranded or double-counted for a migrated-in user.

DEFUSED for the migration surface. Emissions are settled to the block and then frozen for the whole Migrating window, and finalizeAndReset fast-forwards lastRewardTime to now so the frozen gap is never retro-emitted. No Linear-Depletion / rate-drift signature: this staker uses a flat phusdPerSecond, not a depleting-balance rate, so the phoenix Linear-Depletion family does not apply here. (Pre-existing ss9l1 stale-rate-on-revival remains open and is unchanged by this diff.)

DEFUSED despite migrate() having no nonReentrant. Three independent guards: (1) onlyOwner on migrate; (2) both staker entry points it calls (batchMigrate:500, depositFor:628) carry nonReentrant on the staker, so a token callback cannot re-enter the staker mid-flow; (3) `token` is constrained by poolExists on BOTH stakers, so an arbitrary hostile token cannot be routed through unless the owner has already registered it as a pool. The migrator itself holds no persistent state a reentrant call could corrupt — `total`/`migratedCount` are memory-local.

SUPPRESSED per Law 3. Everything is onlyOwner by design and both targets are immutable specifically to remove the compromised-key drain vector (section (B), :27-31). Reporting 'the owner controls migration' would be pure noise. The non-obvious footgun that IS in scope is filed separately as PATTERN-003.
DEFUSED. SafeERC20 forceApprove is used; no raw approve/transfer return value is ignored anywhere in the new contract.
DEFUSED. `data.length < 32` is the correct boundary for 'cannot decode a uint256'. Per the pattern note, not flagging every comparison — checked and correct.

PARTIALLY DEFUSED. The two loops bound on DIFFERENT arrays (`amounts.length` then `users.length`). Against StableStaker V2 they are always equal (batchMigrate:511 allocates `new uint256[](users.length)`). A shorter returned array panics with an out-of-bounds revert — atomic and safe. A LONGER one is the only unsafe direction and is folded into PATTERN-002.
